catalogMeta.title: Thrivefold Real Game Content Catalog — AI, Privacy, Media, Relationships & Pose Verification Extension
catalogMeta.principle: Static JSON defines authored tasks and rules; dynamic engine selects assignments; evidence determines verification; backend determines permanent rewards.
catalogMeta.importantLimit: This is a static content catalog and policy contract, not proof that the referenced AI, secure-storage, MediaPipe, Letters, journal, redaction, or private-record adapters are implemented. Any task requiring a missing capability must be unavailable until that adapter is built and tested. Health-related content requires appropriate review before production.
changeSummary: Added AI verification framework with deterministic gates and optional Bring Your Own Key provider connection tasks.
Added consent-based MediaPipe Pose Landmarker task definitions and explicit runtime-adapter gating.

Added open-letter, selected-media, screenshot-redaction, address privacy, family-image consent, self-discovery, cooking, gardening, faith/values, social/dating, and private adult intimacy settings tasks.
Added presentation tone profiles that never alter task objectives, evidence rules, points, safety or eligibility.
Added explicit sensitive-data rules: no forced exact-address, home-image, family-photo, intimate-history, or broad gallery collection.
Added optional adult private-intimacy record schema with no scoring and no partner identifiers.

implementationStatus.meaning: JSON syntax and custom cross-reference/evidence checks pass. This does not imply formal JSON Schema validation, runtime adapter availability, database integration, or a completed privacy/security review.

assessmentKeyHandling.deploymentRequirement: Keep the companion asset in backend-only storage. Correct answers must be evaluated server-side or through a verified local assessment engine with an appropriately protected answer source; never bundle this server asset into a public client.

ethicalBoundaries.purpose: Support self-directed wellbeing, health literacy, and personal development without judging a person's worth or sensitive identity.
consentRules: Sensitive fields are optional and collected only when a feature has a clear purpose.
Users can skip, edit, disable, or delete optional profile context where legally applicable.
No points or level requirements depend on disclosing religion, sex, sexual history, reproductive status, body measurements, or mental-health details.
Face images, biometric templates, and facial-landmark measurements are not collected by this catalog.
Do not display private health or faith data in public profiles, social feeds, or notifications without separate explicit consent.
verificationHonesty: System-verified means the app can validate the specified digital event, not necessarily an external real-world fact.
Self-reported activity must remain labelled self-reported.
A clinician result manually entered by the user is not independently authenticated unless an actual authorized integration confirms provenance.
No client-side button, local counter, or AI response can independently grant authoritative permanent rewards.

sections.title: Choose what matters
sections.content: A useful goal is defined by the player and linked to a concrete next action.

sections.title: Make the first step small
sections.content: Choose an action that is feasible in current circumstances rather than relying on perfect motivation.

sections.title: Plan for interruptions
sections.content: A flexible backup, pause, or revised goal is a valid response to changing circumstances.

sections.title: What completion proves
sections.content: An app can verify recorded steps; it cannot establish every external event or a person's worth.

sections.title: Compare like with like
sections.content: Check serving size and use the same basis when comparing labels.

sections.title: Consider the whole pattern
sections.content: Food choices should account for variety, adequacy, preference, local availability, and health needs.

sections.title: Respect chosen constraints
sections.content: User-selected restrictions, allergies, and cultural or faith-related food choices must be respected without inferring identity.

sections.title: What BMI is
sections.content: BMI relates body weight to height and is used as a screening measure.

sections.title: What BMI does not measure directly
sections.content: BMI does not directly measure body-fat percentage or distinguish fat, muscle, and bone mass.

sections.title: Use context
sections.content: An individual's interpretation may require other health measures and professional assessment.

sections.title: Clinical measurement
sections.content: Bone mineral density can be measured by tests such as DXA/DEXA when clinically appropriate.

sections.title: Appearance is not a test
sections.content: A person's appearance, face shape, height, or game score cannot establish bone density.

sections.title: Review results in context
sections.content: A qualified healthcare professional interprets results alongside history and other risk factors.

sections.title: Consistent routine
sections.content: Authoritative oral-health guidance commonly recommends regular brushing with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between teeth; individualized dental instructions may differ.

sections.title: Professional care
sections.content: Dental professionals can assess conditions that an app or photograph cannot reliably diagnose.

sections.title: Personalized advice
sections.content: Follow advice from your dental professional for your circumstances.

sections.title: Privacy and choice
sections.content: This optional lesson does not require disclosure of sexual history or orientation.

sections.title: General education
sections.content: The final published lesson must use qualified, reviewed, current sexual-health information appropriate to the user's jurisdiction and age.

sections.title: When to seek care
sections.content: A quiz cannot replace personalized care from a qualified professional.

sections.title: Communicate clearly
sections.content: Use clear communication and respect each person's boundaries.

sections.title: Choice can change
sections.content: A person can pause or withdraw agreement; do not pressure them.

sections.title: No forced disclosure
sections.content: The app never needs to collect a player's sexual history to teach consent.

lessonDefinitions.title: Know Where a Health Record Came From

sections.title: Source matters
sections.content: Distinguish self-entered values, connected-device events, and clinical records.

sections.title: Date and method matter
sections.content: Store a timestamp, units, and measurement method where applicable.

sections.title: Do not overclaim
sections.content: A correctly stored record does not automatically establish a diagnosis.

sections.title: Check the source
sections.content: Look at who made a claim, the evidence offered, its date, and relevant conflicts of interest.

sections.title: Represent uncertainty
sections.content: When evidence is limited, say so instead of turning a guess into a fact.

sections.title: Personal stories have limits
sections.content: Anecdotes can be meaningful but do not prove that a result will apply to everyone.

lessonDefinitions.title: What Body Measurements Can Tell You

sections.title: Record the real source
sections.content: Keep measurement units, date, and source together.

sections.title: No appearance-based estimates
sections.content: Do not infer body-fat percentage or bone density from a photograph, face, or body shape.

sections.title: No body worth score
sections.content: Measurements are optional records, not scores of beauty, morality, or personal worth.

sections.title: Interest is not owed
sections.content: A conversation or invitation is optional for everyone. No reply, a decline, or disengagement must be respected without pressure.

sections.title: Invite without pressure
sections.content: Use one respectful invitation and make declining easy. Do not treat politeness, silence, or uncertainty as consent.

sections.title: Consent can change
sections.content: Consent is voluntary, informed, specific, and ongoing; a person can change their mind at any time.

sections.title: Choose personal safety
sections.content: Meeting someone is optional. If meeting, consider a public venue, independent transport, privacy boundaries, and a plan to leave.

derivedMeasurementDefinitions.name: BMI screening calculation
derivedMeasurementDefinitions.ageRule: Use adult screening interpretation only where applicable for age 20 and older; do not apply adult categories to children or teens.
limitations: BMI is not direct body-fat measurement.
BMI does not distinguish fat, muscle, and bone mass.
Do not infer fat distribution from BMI.
Do not use as diagnosis, beauty score, worth score, task reward, or automatic diet prescription.

derivedMeasurementDefinitions.name: Body-composition entry gate
derivedMeasurementDefinitions.rule: Accept only explicitly entered or actually integrated measurements; leave unknown values null rather than estimating them from photos, height, weight, or face shape.

derivedMeasurementDefinitions.name: Recorded body-fat result
derivedMeasurementDefinitions.rule: No estimate is produced unless a separately validated device integration explicitly supplies it. No photograph-based estimate.

derivedMeasurementDefinitions.name: Recorded bone-density result
derivedMeasurementDefinitions.rule: The app stores the result; clinical interpretation remains with an appropriate healthcare professional.

Task version matches the accepted assignment.
A duplicate submission returns the original result.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies the in-app sequence, not every real-world fact represented by it.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can validate locally; authoritative reward remains provisional until backend acceptance.

verificationPolicies.description: The engine evaluates answers against the static assessment answer key and threshold.
rules: Assessment ID and version must match catalog.
Answers are evaluated by the registered assessment evaluator.
Pass threshold is set in the assessment content.
Retries follow the defined policy.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies answers to this assessment only; not generalized expertise or diagnosis.
verificationPolicies.offline: Offline evaluation allowed for bundled assessments; synchronize result idempotently.

verificationPolicies.description: Checks that required reflection fields are completed without pretending to judge truth or mental health.
rules: Required prompts are answered.
Responses meet bounded format requirements.
Content is not scored for sentiment, morality, religion, gender, or psychological worth.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies completion structure, not factual truth or a clinical state.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can record locally and sync later.

verificationPolicies.description: Records the player's explicit claim that they completed an offline activity.
rules: Player explicitly confirms the event.
Required detail fields are present.
The result remains self-reported unless stronger evidence is available.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Does not independently prove an offline activity.
verificationPolicies.offline: Available offline; status remains self-reported or pending synchronization.

verificationPolicies.description: Validates duration measured by the app's own foreground or permitted session timer.
rules: Elapsed duration is recalculated from recorded events.
Impossible durations and duplicate session IDs are rejected.
Client-supplied total alone is not trusted.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Proves app-recorded elapsed time, not the real-world activity performed during the interval.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can log locally with monotonic timing where supported; synchronize when online.

verificationPolicies.description: Validates the structure and plausible technical range of a measurement record while preserving its provenance.
rules: Units and numeric range are validated.
Source is retained.
Manual values are labeled self-reported.
Connected-device or clinician sources are claimed only when actual integration metadata exists.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Validation does not verify that a manually entered value is true and does not diagnose a condition.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can store locally; authority and integrations reconcile after sync.

verificationPolicies.description: Combines an in-app educational assessment with a short reflection where configured.
rules: Assessment must pass.
Reflection must meet structural criteria.
Only configured eligible rewards are issued.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Does not demonstrate clinical competence.
verificationPolicies.offline: Available if all content and evaluators are bundled; rewards reconcile online.

verificationPolicies.description: Stores a user-entered healthcare record with explicit source attribution.
rules: Required fields and units are validated.
Clinician-origin claims require user declaration or an actual authorized integration.
No result is interpreted as a diagnosis without a suitable validated pathway.
verificationPolicies.limitations: A manually entered clinical result is not independently authenticated by the app.
verificationPolicies.offline: Secure local entry and later sync.

verificationPolicies.description: AI may evaluate a user-authored, non-sensitive artifact against a fixed catalog rubric and return structured advisory findings. It cannot prove real-world actions or act as the sole truth authority.
rules: A registered provider adapter and approved rubric must exist before this policy can run.
The engine validates the AI response against a strict JSON schema and the fixed task rubric.
Required deterministic completion criteria must pass independently of the model output.
The player must be shown the result and acknowledge review where required by the task.
AI confidence or a free-form success assertion alone never grants a reward.
AI cannot verify that an offline event happened, diagnose a condition, infer religion/gender/sexuality/personality from appearance, assess attractiveness, or judge moral worth.

Do not send highly sensitive health, intimacy, address, family-photo, or identity data unless a specific feature has informed, per-operation consent and the registered provider flow explicitly permits it; default is to exclude and redact such data.
Prompts, outputs, rubric version, provider/model IDs, and timestamps may be recorded as minimal audit metadata; do not persist API keys or unnecessary sensitive prompt text.
If the provider is unavailable, response schema is invalid, or the player declines review, the task remains incomplete or pending rather than silently passing.
verificationPolicies.limitations: AI review supports evaluation of submitted content structure or rubric alignment, not factual truth, clinical conclusions, real-world completion, or generalized expertise.
verificationPolicies.offline: Use deterministic local checks offline. AI-assisted review remains pending unless an approved local model adapter is actually installed and the rubric permits it.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that the player explicitly configured an enabled AI provider adapter and completed a minimal live connection test without placing the secret in task evidence.
rules: The provider adapter ID and model must appear in the runtime allowlist.
The API key is entered only in a dedicated masked secret field and is never copied into task evidence, analytics, logs, crash reports, screenshots, or backend records.
On Android/iOS, use the platform secure secret storage adapter when available; for Expo this normally means the installed and configured SecureStore integration.
Never store a raw provider key in catalog JSON, app source, AsyncStorage, general SQLite tables, analytics, or synchronized user-profile data.

On web, do not claim equivalent secure storage. Default to session-memory-only credentials and warn that refresh loses the key; persistent browser storage must not be enabled unless an explicitly reviewed secure-vault design exists.
Use a minimal non-sensitive provider connectivity request and retain only the necessary result metadata, never the secret or an unnecessary full response.
A key is valid only for the selected provider and tested connection; the task does not promise provider free usage or free model access.
If the adapter is not implemented, a request fails, the device is offline, or secure storage fails, do not award connection-verification rewards.
Key deletion/rotation must remove the stored credential and invalidate any cached authorization state.
verificationPolicies.limitations: This verifies a configured connection, not the safety of a provider, the user billing status, unlimited quota, or the accuracy of its responses.
verificationPolicies.offline: The user may read setup guidance offline; connection verification and its reward remain pending until the selected provider actually responds.

verificationPolicies.description: Uses a registered on-device pose-landmark adapter to evaluate a task-specific movement pattern from a short, consented camera session.
rules: Do not offer system-verified landmark completion until an actual native/runtime adapter and licensed model asset are installed, tested, and registered.
Ask for camera permission only when the player starts this optional task and explain exactly what is processed.
Where supported, process frames locally and keep raw frames in memory only; do not save or upload video by default.
Store only the minimal task-specific derived metrics needed for validation, not full landmark histories or body images.
Validate frame count, confidence thresholds, event ordering, timestamp monotonicity, and task-specific movement criteria using deterministic code.
Pose landmarks can support visible pose or repetition checkpoints; they cannot diagnose injury, pain, bone density, body-fat percentage, or overall fitness.
Poor framing, accessibility needs, or model uncertainty must offer a no-camera alternative with honest self-reported/evidence-supported status.
No face recognition, identity matching, emotion inference, attractiveness scoring, or unrelated surveillance.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Pose landmarks estimate observable joint landmarks and movement patterns under model and camera constraints. They do not prove every real-world action or medical safety.
verificationPolicies.offline: Local inference may run offline only when the model and adapter are installed. Sync compact verified metrics and consent/audit metadata; do not upload raw frames by default.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that the player reviewed sharing scope and selected a specific media item or screenshot through an operating-system picker, if they choose to attach one.
rules: Media attachment is optional unless a specific feature has a clearly explained need; an equivalent text-only path must exist for ordinary game progress.
Prefer platform photo/document pickers that grant access only to assets selected by the player; do not request broad gallery access for task verification.
Display the selected asset and intended audience before any upload or publication.
Strip EXIF geolocation and unnecessary metadata before sharing; show a preview and explain where the item will go.
Do not require exact home addresses, private home interiors, family images, ID documents, intimate images, or identifiable third-party data to earn points.
The player must explicitly confirm every upload/publication. Drafting, selecting, or previewing media does not automatically publish it.
Only record a successful share if the actual share/publish operation succeeds and the user selected that audience.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies picker/consent/share workflow events, not the truth or appropriateness of an image or the consent of every person depicted.
verificationPolicies.offline: A local private attachment can be saved locally if the feature supports it; cloud/public sharing waits for explicit confirmation and connectivity.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that an open-letter draft is saved and the player reviewed privacy and audience settings. Publication is optional and separate.
rules: Saving a private draft is sufficient for the basic writing task; publication is not required for points.
Anonymous publication is only available if the existing Letters feature provides real anonymity controls and moderation/safety support.
Never describe a post as anonymous if the backend retains identifying metadata that is visible to recipients or moderators under its policy.
Warn the player to remove names, addresses, workplace/school details, private health details, and third-party secrets before public sharing.
Publication requires a separate, explicit confirmation after preview; changing a draft never silently republishes it.
publishConsentEventId is required only for an actual publish action; private draft or keep-private outcomes must not manufacture a publish event.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies saved draft and workflow choices, not the factual accuracy of the letter or that anonymous identity can never be discovered.
verificationPolicies.offline: Save a private draft locally when supported. Online publication remains pending until the existing Letters backend confirms it.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that a private-record feature is opt-in, access-scoped, and has visible export/delete controls before optional entries are made.
rules: The task can be completed by reviewing or configuring privacy controls; it must not require disclosing intimate or medical facts.
Sensitive records must be separated from public profile data, achievements, leaderboards, and ordinary coaching prompts.
Default AI processing of sensitive private records is disabled.
The player can skip, edit, export where supported, and delete optional records according to product policy and law.
No reward is tied to how many sexual encounters, partners, health conditions, or personal disclosures the player records.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies app privacy settings and UI/domain events, not an external guarantee that no device-level compromise is possible.
verificationPolicies.offline: Review and local settings may be completed offline; deletion/sync state is reconciled when the backend is available.

verificationPolicies.description: Records a voluntary social action or date-planning activity without claiming to verify another person response or consent.
rules: The player chooses whether to plan, invite, attend, or reflect; a date, romantic outcome, sexual encounter, or another person saying yes is never required.
Tasks require respectful, non-coercive communication and acceptance of refusal.
Meeting a stranger is never required. If the player elects to meet someone, offer an optional public-location and check-in safety plan.
Do not collect another person identity, exact address, contact details, or intimate information as proof.
The result remains self-reported for real-world actions.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Does not independently verify that a real-world conversation or date occurred.
verificationPolicies.offline: May be completed offline as a clearly self-reported event and synchronized idempotently.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies explicit provider/privacy preferences without requiring a key or sensitive prompt.
rules: Provider choice must refer to a registered provider or explicit disabled/no-AI state.
Store preferences as user-controlled settings.
No API key is required for this task.
Do not send a prompt to a provider as part of this review.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies saved settings, not provider safety or data-retention guarantees.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can be completed offline and synchronized idempotently.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies a completed in-app privacy review and saved decisions.
rules: Review topics and choices must be registered by the application.
The user may choose no change or decline an optional feature.
No address, image, health detail, or other sensitive value is required.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies review events, not absolute privacy against device compromise.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can be completed offline where settings can be saved locally.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies review of media access or a third-party sharing decision without requiring an actual uploaded image.
rules: No media file is required for a settings/privacy review.
The picker should scope access to player-selected assets.
Sharing decisions must be explicit and may be do-not-share or keep-private.
No broad gallery permission is required for task completion.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies in-app review choices, not permission or consent from every person depicted in a separate image.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can be completed offline.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies completion of a redaction exercise using a synthetic or non-sensitive screenshot.
rules: Use synthetic or clearly non-sensitive source content.
The configured redaction UI must apply redaction before saving the derived preview.
Do not claim automated scanning catches every secret.
No real sensitive source screenshot must be uploaded.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies an exercise, not a guarantee that every possible sensitive detail was found.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can run offline with a bundled synthetic fixture.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies a review of optional trusted-contact controls.
rules: Do not require contact import or exact address.
Declining the feature is a valid outcome.
Only actual saved settings can satisfy the policy.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Does not authenticate the identity or availability of a contact.
verificationPolicies.offline: May be reviewed offline; backend sync reconciles settings later.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies review, replacement, or removal of a BYOK credential through the registered secure-storage adapter.
rules: Only allowlisted provider adapters are available.
Never return credential material as evidence.
For removal, validate that the app can no longer retrieve the stored credential.
For rotation, verify the new connection before clearing a working credential unless user explicitly confirms removal.
No successful live provider request means no claim that connection works.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies app credential-management operations, not account-level revocation by the provider unless that external action is confirmed.
verificationPolicies.offline: Removal can run offline locally; online provider revocation/connectivity may remain pending.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that the player reviewed and consented to a supported optional local pose-landmark setup.
rules: The registered adapter and model must actually be available.
Camera consent is captured at feature use, never assumed from prior permission.
Raw frames must not be retained and upload must not be attempted by default.
If required adapter is missing, this policy cannot pass; the task must be hidden or replaced with a non-camera task.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies feature configuration/consent, not movement quality or medical suitability.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can validate local model readiness offline.

verificationPolicies.description: Verifies that an assigned special quest has satisfied its configured child-task completion rule.
rules: The child task must be an allowed taskId in the assigned quest snapshot.
The child assignment must have passed its own registered verification policy.
The parent quest does not re-award the child task’s points or XP unless a separate explicitly configured quest bonus exists.
Duplicate child events return the same quest result.
A self-reported child task stays self-reported and cannot be promoted to system-verified by the parent quest.
verificationPolicies.limitations: Verifies the relation between a quest and a qualifying child completion; it does not independently verify the underlying real-world action.
verificationPolicies.offline: Can evaluate a local provisional quest state offline; permanent reward authority reconciles with backend.

dailyGoalTargetProfiles.description: Low-demand target for days when the player prefers a light plan.
Default illustrative target; assign only after user preferences and eligible task availability are considered.
Optional higher target chosen by the player, never imposed automatically after leveling.

rules: Task points, daily goal points, XP, and skill XP are separate quantities.
Daily progress is calculated from eligible accepted completion events for the player's game date.
Skipping, selecting, opening, starting, or abandoning a task earns zero points.
Only catalog-configured eligible completions contribute to the daily target.
A daily completion reward is awarded once per game date and target-policy version.
Rewards are fixed at assignment time using task and policy versions.
Client-submitted points and XP are never authoritative.
Over-target points may be recorded in event history but daily-goal completion remains one-time.
Repeatable tasks require fresh evidence and a defined recurrence window.
No points are awarded for religion, gender, sexual activity, weight loss, body-fat change, appearance, or sensitive disclosure.
pointEconomy.targetSnapshot: Persist the selected target, local game date, time-zone ID, policy version, and assignment set; do not raise the target retroactively after the player earns points.
pointEconomy.dailyRollover: Use the player's stored IANA time-zone identifier. Reconcile late offline events to their recorded game date using trusted timestamps and defined offline policy; do not trust an arbitrary client total.
pointEconomy.example: If the target is 40 and eligible completions sum to 25, accepting a special quest changes nothing. A verified 15-point quest makes progress 40/40. A 10-point quest makes it 35/40. Skipping never increases progress.

stateTransitions.awards: Only configured eligible task points, XP, and skill XP; idempotently.

requirements: Store original assignment ID, new replacement assignment ID, task/version, timestamps, and transition audit event.
A replacement must be an eligible distinct assignment; do not rename the original task and mark it complete.
The engine offers relevant special quests from the static catalog.
No penalty for skipping or choosing rest.
No reward from a skip, reroll, acceptance, start, abandonment, or duplicate submission.
Once accepted, the task identity, evidence policy, and reward snapshot remain stable.
A stale submission from a skipped assignment cannot be accepted unless the state machine explicitly permits restoration.
Do not impose arbitrary punitive skip limits; block farming through assignment identity, eligibility, recurrence, fresh evidence, and idempotency.

dailyTaskRules.assignmentSource: taskDefinitions and specialQuestDefinitions in this catalog
dailyTaskRules.assignmentSelection: Deterministic eligibility filter first, then player-goal and task-selection ranking; save the resulting assignment snapshot.
rules: Do not assign tasks whose eligibility, safety, prerequisite, or optional-feature constraints fail.
Never use gender alone to select reproductive or anatomy-specific tasks.
Do not force body measurement, food tracking, mental-health disclosure, faith disclosure, or sexual-health education.
Avoid assigning the same task repeatedly without a valid recurrence rule and fresh evidence.
Keep the same daily assignment after refresh and app restart.
The player may skip today and choose an eligible special quest.
The daily target snapshot remains stable for the game date unless the player explicitly changes a permitted plan setting; a change cannot erase or fabricate existing points.
dailyTaskRules.dailyContributionFormula: Sum accepted, eligible point ledger contributions for the player's game date and target policy. UI progress is min(sum, target); ledger retains underlying legitimate contributions.
dailyTaskRules.pendingEvidence: Pending, rejected, skipped, or unverified claims do not contribute authoritative points unless the task's explicit self-report policy permits provisional display; provisional values must be labelled and reconciled.
dailyTaskRules.selectionSeed: Persist deterministic selection seed and catalog/ruleset versions for reproducibility. Do not reroll on screen refresh.

chapterDefinitions.title: Foundations & Self-Knowledge
chapterDefinitions.description: Set personal goals, identify preferences, and start with realistic actions.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Build self-directed goals and a reliable baseline.

chapterDefinitions.title: Habits That Fit Real Life
chapterDefinitions.description: Design flexible habits and plan for barriers instead of demanding perfect streaks.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Build adaptable routines and recovery plans.

chapterDefinitions.title: Sleep & Recovery
chapterDefinitions.description: Record patterns, develop a chosen wind-down routine, and respond to recovery needs.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Understand and adapt personal sleep and recovery routines.

chapterDefinitions.title: Movement & Mobility
chapterDefinitions.description: Plan accessible activity, record actual sessions, and learn safe adaptations.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Develop sustainable movement and mobility practices.

chapterDefinitions.title: Strength & Function
chapterDefinitions.description: Understand movement choices, recovery, and functional capacity.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Practice appropriate strength and function habits.

chapterDefinitions.title: Food Literacy
chapterDefinitions.description: Learn how to compare food information and make informed choices.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Improve practical nutrition literacy.

chapterDefinitions.title: Food That Fits
chapterDefinitions.description: Turn real preferences, availability, budget, and cultural constraints into usable meal plans.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Plan food in a way that respects access and preference.

chapterDefinitions.title: Health Data & Evidence
chapterDefinitions.description: Understand sources, measurements, and their limitations.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Read health information without overclaiming certainty.

chapterDefinitions.title: Oral & Personal Care
chapterDefinitions.description: Build user-chosen personal care routines and prepare for professional care.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Maintain sustainable personal-care practices.

chapterDefinitions.title: Emotional Skills
chapterDefinitions.description: Practice reflection and optional grounding without turning feelings into diagnoses.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Use chosen reflection and coping tools appropriately.

chapterDefinitions.title: Focus & Learning
chapterDefinitions.description: Practice learning, assessment, creative work, and decision-making.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Demonstrate understanding and apply it to a meaningful next step.

chapterDefinitions.title: Connection & Boundaries
chapterDefinitions.description: Set boundaries and choose connection or quiet according to your needs.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Build communication and relationship skills.

chapterDefinitions.title: Values & Culture
chapterDefinitions.description: Honor self-chosen values and cultural preferences without ranking identity.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Align daily choices with values the player chooses to share.

chapterDefinitions.title: Planning & Time
chapterDefinitions.description: Review commitments, make plans, and adjust them when reality changes.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Plan with flexibility and realistic expectations.

chapterDefinitions.title: Body Respect & Self-Care
chapterDefinitions.description: Track optional measurements and care preferences without rating attractiveness or worth.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Support body agency and interpretation of measurements.

chapterDefinitions.title: Preventive Care & Records
chapterDefinitions.description: Prepare for appointments and maintain records the user chooses to keep.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Improve readiness for appropriate professional care.

chapterDefinitions.title: Adaptation & Access
chapterDefinitions.description: Adapt goals to energy, access, disability, and changing circumstances.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Keep progress possible without requiring one specific body or lifestyle.

chapterDefinitions.title: Integrated Wellbeing
chapterDefinitions.description: Bring together selected skills into a coherent personal plan.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Combine chosen areas of growth without forcing irrelevant health modules.

chapterDefinitions.title: Independent Coaching
chapterDefinitions.description: Review the evidence behind progress and choose the next useful action.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Use the engine as a coach rather than depending on prompts or streaks.

chapterDefinitions.title: Long-Term Personal Design
chapterDefinitions.description: Maintain a sustainable, self-authored development plan with real milestones.
chapterDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Create a realistic continuing plan and understand its limitations.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Understand the chapter's purpose and choose a personally relevant starting point.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Earn XP from valid tasks; orientation does not create automatic completion.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Practice the basics with explicit instructions and realistic alternatives.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Only eligible task awards contribute XP.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Apply a learned skill in a suitable real context and reflect on evidence.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Existing completions cannot be replayed for duplicate rewards.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Plan and execute a chosen action with less scaffolding where suitable.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Evidence and task eligibility remain mandatory.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Adjust an approach based on experience, constraints, or new information.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Changing or pausing a goal may be a valid outcome.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Review chapter evidence and prepare for a meaningful checkpoint.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: No repetition-only requirement; use valid task evidence and reflection.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Complete a real chapter checkpoint selected from eligible alternatives.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: The chapter checkpoint must be accepted; no sensitive task is mandatory.

levelStageDefinitions.purpose: Demonstrate long-term self-coaching, evidence literacy, and a sustainable continuation plan.
levelStageDefinitions.rule: Requires actual progression and an explicit final review; it is not a decorative badge.

levelProgressionRules.levelSemantics: A level is earned game progression, not a task and not a claim of health status, beauty, morality, or personal worth.
levelProgressionRules.xpRequiredToAdvance: Explicitly stored on each level record; computed once when the static catalog is authored and then validated. Runtime does not invent level content.
levelProgressionRules.chapterMilestones: Every 50 levels has a real chapter checkpoint linked to authored content. The player can select eligible alternatives when a task is irrelevant or inaccessible.
noRepetitionInflation: No task is created merely by changing an integer in its name.
The level manifest is separate from the task catalog.
Previously awarded completion IDs do not award XP again.
Repeated practice grants rewards only when the task's recurrence policy permits fresh evidence.
Sensitive or demographic disclosures are never required to advance general levels.
levelProgressionRules.finalLevel: Level 1000 requires real accumulated XP and final sustainable mastery review. Do not display completion if the final requirements are not met.

levelDefinitions.title: Thrivefold — Level 1000: Sustainable Mastery
levelDefinitions.purpose: Complete the final long-term personal development review and demonstrate sustained, evidence-backed use of selected skills.
levelDefinitions.primaryOutcome: Create a self-authored continuing plan that identifies real progress, limits of the available evidence, and a practical path beyond the game.
levelDefinitions.note: Final level completion requires the final challenge plus valid progression; no fake post-level XP or infinite content is implied.

selectionSteps: Filter inactive or unreviewed production content.
Filter eligibility, age gates, user consent, prerequisite, recurrence, and safety constraints.
Exclude already-completed non-repeatable tasks and tasks that would duplicate active assignments.
Rank remaining tasks by the player's explicitly selected goals, relevant verified skill outcomes, time, accessibility, and prior task feedback.
Offer a stable eligible task list with reasons.
Persist assignment, catalog version, policy version, selection seed, and rationale codes.
If a task is skipped, offer a distinct eligible special quest or alternative task.
Use deterministic rules when AI or network is unavailable.
coachingRules.aiBoundary: AI may explain authored content or summarize actual saved events; it cannot create production tasks, determine verification outcomes, set points, or override eligibility.

clientProjectionMayContain: non-secret rules required for offline display
clientProjectionRules.requirement: Build a sanitized client projection that strips serverOnlyAssessmentKeys; server verifies quizzes and permanent rewards. Do not import the complete source catalog into the mobile/web client bundle.

rules: Use durable local storage and transactional writes where supported.
Store evidence provenance, catalog/policy versions, assignment IDs, and stable operation IDs.
Offline records may remain locally recorded or pending; do not mislabel them server-confirmed.
Backend validates ownership, current state, policy, prerequisites, reward eligibility, and idempotency.
Duplicate and concurrent requests must not duplicate permanent rewards.
Local counters are projections, never the permanent authority.
Rejected records remain inspectable with an explanation and are not silently erased.
Sensitive measurements, faith preferences, and sexual/reproductive context remain private and access-controlled.

additionalMandatoryChecks: Every AI task requires a registered runtime provider adapter; no mock success or placeholder adapter may be released.
BYOK secrets never appear in task evidence, JSON, telemetry, logs, synchronized profile records, or crash reports.
Web BYOK never claims secure persistence without a reviewed secure-vault implementation.
Pose-landmark tasks are unavailable until native adapter/model, offline behavior, permission timing, and raw-frame retention tests pass.
Sensitive media tasks use single-item selection and never require exact home addresses or family/intimate photos.
Adult intimacy record schema and screens remain optional, private, age-gated, and completely excluded from progression scoring.
AI-assisted verification never alone validates real-world events or diagnoses.
Never ship serverOnlyAssessmentKeys in any public/client bundle; generate a client-safe catalog projection and keep the answer key in server-only storage.
Assessment references must resolve to authored questions, pass thresholds, and server-side answer keys.
Conditional publish-consent evidence is required only if an actual publication occurs; a private letter task must remain completable without publishing.
Review-only media tasks must not require a media upload or selected asset.
A photo attachment task that uses the selected-media policy must require an actually selected asset for that task; users may skip the entire task without penalty.

guidanceReferences.title: CDC: About Body Mass Index (BMI)
guidanceReferences.usage: Use to explain BMI as a screening measure that does not distinguish fat, muscle, and bone; do not treat it as a diagnosis.

guidanceReferences.title: WHO: Physical activity
guidanceReferences.usage: General source for accessible physical-activity education; personalize safely and do not prescribe a universal workout to every user.

guidanceReferences.title: WHO: Healthy diet, 26 January 2026
guidanceReferences.usage: Use broad principles of adequacy, balance, moderation, diversity and cultural context; avoid inflexible prescriptions.

guidanceReferences.title: NIAMS: Bone Mineral Density Tests — What the Numbers Mean
guidanceReferences.usage: Bone-density tests and results require appropriate clinical interpretation; do not infer bone density from appearance.

guidanceReferences.title: CDC: Oral Health Tips for Adults
guidanceReferences.usage: Use for reviewed oral-health education; individual dental instructions may differ.

guidanceReferences.title: American Dental Association: Home Oral Care
guidanceReferences.usage: Use for reviewed oral-care education, with professional advice for individual needs.

guidanceReferences.title: NIMH: My Mental Health — Do I Need Help?
guidanceReferences.usage: Use for carefully reviewed non-diagnostic wellbeing resources and professional-support signposting.

guidanceReferences.title: Expo SecureStore (SDK 55 documentation)
guidanceReferences.usage: Reference for encrypted small key/value secret storage using Android Keystore-backed storage and iOS Keychain. Must be installed/configured and tested in the actual project; not a reason to store keys in general app storage.

guidanceReferences.title: Expo authentication guide: storing data
guidanceReferences.usage: Clarifies that Expo SecureStore is a native-platform feature and there is no equivalent web functionality; web BYOK persistence must not be assumed secure.

guidanceReferences.title: Android Developers: Security tips
guidanceReferences.usage: Treat API keys as sensitive credentials; do not commit them or expose them to clients/backend logs; use layered protection.

guidanceReferences.title: Google AI Edge: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker options
guidanceReferences.usage: Pose Landmarker supports image, video, and live-stream modes with confidence thresholds. A real mobile/native adapter and model asset are still required; JSON alone does not implement it.

privateRecordSchemas.title: Optional private adult intimacy journal

restrictions: No phone, email, social handle, contact ID, exact address, or identifying photo
store locally encrypted when implemented; sync separately opt-in

storagePolicy.aiProcessing: disabled_by_default; never automatically sent to BYOK or server AI
storagePolicy.exports: explicit user action and preview required
storagePolicy.deletion: user-accessible delete control; deletion results reconciled with backend if sync has been enabled

scorePolicy.reason: Disclosure or tracking of sexual history, dates, encounters, partner count, or duration never affects game progress.

privateRecordSchemas.verification: All entries remain self-reported; no partner identity or sexual activity is independently verified.

requiredFlow.rule: Check task ID/version, user consent, age eligibility, and allowed artifact type.
Create a preview and remove unnecessary names, exact location, account secrets, family images, intimate records, and unrelated health information.
Use only an installed and allowlisted provider/model adapter; a model name typed by the user alone is not enough.
Show which provider receives the submitted content, provider settings/billing caveat, and whether content may leave the device; require explicit confirmation.
Send only task-appropriate minimum inputs with a fixed rubric and strict output schema.
Validate returned JSON, rubric ID/version, bounded values, and required fields; reject malformed responses.
Run domain-engine rules separately. The model cannot override a failed prerequisite, evidence rule, safety check, eligibility rule, or server authorization.
Show the feedback and allow accept, edit, dismiss, or request another review. AI output is advice, not a fact by default.
Only the registered task policy plus authoritative backend acceptance can award permanent progression.
Store minimal provider/model/rubric/version/result metadata; do not log API keys; expose review/delete controls for AI artifacts.

allowedUses: check required fields in user-authored plans
evaluate a non-sensitive artifact against a fixed, versioned rubric
summarize records already provided by the user with provenance
help compare a plan against explicit user-stated constraints
prohibitedUses: claiming an offline real-world action happened
diagnosing or treating medical/mental conditions
inferring religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, personality, morality, consent, or medical status from face/body/photos
rating beauty, face structure, body shape, skin color, teeth whiteness, fatness, bone density, or human worth
scoring sexual acts, partner count, first/recent sex, intimate duration, or sensitive disclosure
automatic publication or sending a letter without preview and confirmation
bypassing deterministic verification or granting rewards by itself
processing private intimacy journal entries by default
aiVerificationFramework.offlineBehavior: The deterministic game engine remains usable. AI-based review remains pending or unavailable unless an approved local model adapter is installed; do not fabricate a pass.

keyStorage.mobile: Use the actual platform secure-store adapter (Expo SecureStore on supported native platforms if installed/configured). Store only small secrets; handle keychain/keystore failures explicitly.
keyStorage.web: No equivalent secure store is assumed. Default to session-memory-only credentials. Never persist a raw key in localStorage or include it in sync; do not claim secure persistent BYOK on web without a separately reviewed implementation.
keyStorage.server: BYOK keys must not be transmitted to Thrivefold backend or included in task/telemetry/crash events. Server-configured provider secrets are a separate server-admin feature.
keyStorage.logs: Redact authorization headers, request URLs containing secrets, provider errors, prompt values that may include sensitive data, and crash breadcrumbs.
keyStorage.revocation: Provide remove/revoke action, clear in-memory caches, and require a fresh test after replacement.

capabilities: estimate task-specific joint angles or repetition events where the registered implementation supports them
summarize landmark confidence and valid frame count
nonCapabilities: measure bone density or body fat
prove that a user performed an activity whenever the person is out of frame
availabilityGate: camera permission is requested only at feature use
privacy test confirms raw frames are not persisted/uploaded by default
poseLandmarkVerification.ifUnavailable: Hide pose-verified reward pathway and offer an honestly classified no-camera alternative; never treat manual confirmation as landmark-verified.

exactAddress.collection: never required for a game task
exactAddress.use: only a separate user-triggered feature with clear necessity and consent

homeAndFamilyPhotos.picker: use OS single-item picker where possible
homeAndFamilyPhotos.thirdParties: consider consent and privacy before sharing
homeAndFamilyPhotos.metadata: strip EXIF geolocation and unnecessary metadata before upload

screenshots.redaction: remove addresses, names, access tokens, health records, intimate details, and private conversations before any share
screenshots.secretDetection: registered deterministic scanner may warn but does not guarantee all sensitive content was found

sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.galleryPermission: Do not request broad all-gallery permission merely to complete quests or verify progress. Ask for access only for a distinct feature with a clear need; prefer platform pickers for selected assets.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.cameraPermission: Request only when an explicitly selected camera task begins; provide a no-camera alternative wherever the objective permits.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.preciseLocation: Off by default; never collect exact location as a reward condition. If a separate user-requested safety/navigation feature needs it, explain purpose and retention and require a separate permission flow.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.contacts: Never import or scrape address books, match partners, or collect another person’s contact details as a task. Use a user-created private alias for optional journals.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.privateHealthAndIntimacy: High-sensitivity records separated from game points, public profiles, normal coaching, and analytics. Explicit opt-in per feature; cloud sync requires separate consent and security review.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.thirdPartyData: Tasks must not pressure users to upload private messages, partner identities, family photos, home interiors, or another person’s health information.
sensitiveDataAndMediaPolicy.productionRequirement: Enforce this policy in UI, runtime capabilities, database RLS, sync, telemetry, and backend endpoints; JSON alone is not an access-control boundary.

inputsAllowed: relevant user-recorded measurements with source and date
inputsProhibitedAsSoleBasis: personality guess from text or face
rules: Use experience scope to hide irrelevant modules but do not assume anatomy from gender.
Use explicit goals to offer cooking, gardening, faith practice, dating, social, sexual-health education, or solitude tasks; none is mandatory by sex or religion.

Health conditions such as thyroid disease, pain, pregnancy, or other disclosed context must not trigger a diagnosis. Offer user-controlled adjustments and clinician-question preparation; do not prescribe or modify medication.
Do not require a person to be liberal, religious, sexually active, abstinent, dating, married, heterosexual, or socially outgoing.
Offer private, opt-in tasks and safe equivalents; no reward depends on another person’s response or intimate details.
Show why a task was recommended and allow correcting the assumptions used.
taskPersonalizationRules.toneRule: Tone profiles alter wording only. They never change objective, required evidence, points, consent, eligibility, safety, or privacy.

rules: Every field is optional and may remain empty.

Sexual activity, first-time sex, most recent sex, partner count, and duration never earn task points, XP, skill XP, achievements, streaks, or leaderboard status.
No default AI processing, analytics capture, notification text, or public profile display for these records.
Keep local encrypted storage as the default where implemented; cloud sync requires separately explained opt-in.
Tasks may teach consent, safer-sex literacy, healthcare preparation, boundaries, and privacy, but do not tell users to obtain a hookup, target strangers, or have sex.
Dating/social tasks are optional, reward completion of a plan or learning objective, and never depend on a person accepting an invitation.
intimacyAndRelationshipRules.relationshipSupportBoundary: Thrivefold may offer reflection prompts and communication practice but must not present an AI as a licensed therapist or marriage counselor. runtimeCapabilityRegistry.fallback: Never label an unsupported capability as verified. Offer a relevant, accurately classified alternate task or hide the task until implemented.

rules: A special quest selects/assigns an eligible child task from its listed taskIds.
The child task must pass its own verification policy.
The child task award is the sole source of taskPoints, XP, and skill XP unless a separately authored quest bonus is configured and validated.
The quest-parent completion event never duplicates child rewards.
Daily point contribution uses the child task’s frozen reward snapshot and eligible date, not both parent and child values.
Quest acceptance, skip, replacement, or abandonment awards nothing.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: A deterministic app/backend event or registered evaluator passed its explicit rules. The verified scope is only what the evidence proves.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only after applicable authoritative reward processing.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: Evidence met format and rubric requirements, but the app cannot independently establish every real-world claim.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only under the task policy; present limitations plainly.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: The player attested to an offline or external action that the app cannot independently prove.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only if the catalog explicitly permits self-reported reward; never label it system-verified.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: A registered AI adapter reviewed a user-authored artifact against a fixed rubric; deterministic rules still govern eligibility and completion.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: AI output never awards authoritative progress by itself.

verificationClassDefinitions.meaning: An installed on-device sensor/model generated task-specific evidence with recorded confidence and limitations.
verificationClassDefinitions.mayAward: Only for the specified detectable signal; not a medical diagnosis or proof beyond the model’s capability.

newFeatureAcceptanceTests.assertion: AI provider adapter must be registered and make a real non-sensitive connection test; no mocked success.
BYOK secret never appears in task evidence, logs, telemetry, analytics, prompts sent to another provider, or backend profile records.
AI review cannot verify external real-world activities or independently award XP/points.
Pose-landmark task is unavailable unless the installed model, native adapter, camera consent, and deterministic movement evaluator are available.
Raw frames/video are not retained or uploaded by default; confidence failures offer a non-camera alternative.
Exact address, home images, family photos, contacts, and private sexual-history fields are never required for task completion or rewards.
Media use is scoped to selected assets; preview and explicit audience consent precede sharing; upload metadata is sanitized.
Private intimacy history is adult-only, explicit opt-in, zero-score, excluded from AI by default, and stores no third-party identifying data.
Changing tone profile changes only copy, not tasks, evidence, points, privacy, safety, or eligibility.
Social/dating tasks reward a qualifying plan or learning objective, never another person’s response, consent, or sexual activity.
